chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three (characteristics); whoever possesses them is a hypocrite, even if he fasts and prays and claims that he is a Muslim.'
He who, when entrusted, betrays; and when he narrates, lies; and when he promises, breaks his promise.
Surely Allah does not love the treacherous.
Then the Curse of Allah be on him if he was one of the liars.
And mention Ismail in the Book; he was truthful in (his) promise, and he was a Messenger, a Prophet.
ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of a hypocrite in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi identifies betrayal, lying, and broken promises as the core markers of hypocrisy, asserting that these traits invalidate one's claim to Islam regardless of ritual observance. It explicitly links these moral failings to Quranic descriptions of divine displeasure and curses, while contrasting them with the exemplary truthfulness of Prophet Ismail (AS). This triad serves as a critical ethical framework in Shia scholarship for distinguishing between outward piety and inner sincerity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abdu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Three (things), the one who has these in him, would be a hypocrite, and even if he were to Fast, and pray Salāt, and claims that he is a Muslim.
The one who, when entrusted, betrays, when he narrates, lies, and when he promises, breaks.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying in Hisazwj Book [8:58] surely Allah does not love the treacherous.
And Heazwj Said [24:7] then the Curse of Allah be on him if he was one of the liars.
And in the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [19:54] And mention Ismail in the Book; he was truthful in (his) promise, and he was a Rasool, a Prophet’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from certain individuals of his people from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘There are three things that on being found in a person prove him to be a hypocrite, even though he may fast, pray and think that he is a Muslim:
Violation of trust when he is thought of as trustworthy, lying in one’s words and disregard of one’s promises.
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said in His book, ‘. . . Allah does not love the treacherous ones’, [8:58]
also in His words, ‘. . . let Allah’s condemnation be upon him if he lies’ [24:7],
and in the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘Mention in the Book (the Quran) the story of Ishmael; he was true to his promise, a Messenger and a Prophet.’” [19:54]
